summary: Volley renderer (27 E6b, M-31). powerLink's act docks every member's tender together: cmd.act takes a slot or a list of slots; the art's shuttleSlots().docking is a bit mask; the stage's ds= takes a comma list (ds=1,3). The interpreter's nameVolley opens one turn per VolleyTurn, VOLLEY_TURN_MS apart from the claim. Each turn shows its plates with the member event's note, then names its drawn captains (agent/support/holder parts). Those names fold on the turn's own window (castLabels' turn crew flag) though the ships stay parked. The last turn holds to the end of the land and lingers. A turn ends a fade early when the next would pass ATTENTION_MAX. There is a new volleys() test hook, a gallery cell ('Merged · two tenders dock') and stills. Folded in (2026-11-02 Decisions row): 15 §7's short-form numbers are fixed (disperse 3780, stretch 2020 ms, echo 1800→3820, disperse 3780→5800), and pacingBuilt's 'E1 to E5 unchanged' test now compares against fixed rows (pacing-built.json at 3d4e402, 48 rows, identical to cc89afb's non-E6 rows).

deviations: 03 (normative) changed; call it out in the block note. §stage codes: ds= takes a list (ds=1,3); a slot at or past the cap is dropped, and a malformed list does not decode. Per-slot acts: an act's slot may be a list (dock docks every one; launch and operate take the first). §10 test hooks: volleys().
The art's StationState.dockSlot is renamed dockMask, and shuttleSlots().docking is now a bit mask (0 = none), not a slot index.
castLabels' Crew gains a turn flag: a turn's name folds on its own window (the min of the flight's and the window's), not when the sortie leaves.
volleys().people counts the turn names that are captains drawn at the volley's start, so the e2e checks named ≥ people, not an exact list.
The volley e2e case samples in the page every animation frame (a rAF recorder) rather than in a Playwright loop: the loop missed a name under parallel load.
No 15 constant changed (no new values). Only the §7 merge row's What you see and the volley paragraph's numbers. docTables passes.
limitations: A captain held back by a protect (busy elsewhere at the volley's start) can miss their turn's name; History still names them.
A name-only turn (overflow past four labels) marks no History row of its own.
Per-person order across fused beats is not guarded beyond B-15's pieces (as E6a recorded).
